title: Your first session with CLIO Coder
description: Connect a model, open a repository, and ask CLIO Coder to explain how it builds and runs its tests.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Desktop or terminal: find your workspace
description: See both interfaces, learn how to launch them, and choose where to start your next coding session.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Let CLIO Coder work without watching every call
description: Check the sandbox, undo a change with /rewind, tell the safety judge about your machine, and know when yolo is the right call.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Run a playbook from plan to commit
description: Run the builtin sdlc playbook on one task, watch it work, and read the three commits it makes on your branch.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Run it unattended within limits
description: Start a headless run with a cost ceiling and a timeout, ask read-only questions, schedule turns, and know what stops each one.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: See what a session cost and what a run did
description: Read session cost and stop reasons from local journals, verify a sealed record, and prepare an archive that uploads nothing.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: A numerical change, checked with CLIO Coder
description: Follow a temperature-conversion example through a floating-point test failure, a correction, and recorded verification.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Choose a model for your project
description: Connect a local server, a cloud API, or a supported subscription route, then choose models separately for conversation and delegated work.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Coordinate the coding agents you already use
description: Use supported coding peers for bounded assignments, distinguish managed runs from interactive handoffs, and review the results before combining them.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Keep a long coding task on track
description: Inspect context, preserve decisions through a handoff, and resume the correct branch without turning every past message into a current instruction.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Check a change against your repository
description: Declare which checks matter, run them through verification, and inspect whether passing results still match the files you are reviewing.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Add skills and plugins deliberately
description: Preview a project skill or plugin, inspect its package pin, and load only what your task needs; installing is not a permission grant.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Work from a laptop with remote workers
description: Use a local CLIO Coder session to coordinate SSH workers when your machines share the required project path, runtime version, and approved access.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Write an extension with declared capabilities
description: Scaffold, test, and install a small extension, and see exactly what approving its capabilities covers.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Diffusion models in the terminal
description: Connect Inception's Mercury models for chat and workers, and watch an answer refine as a whole instead of arriving token by token.
author: The CLIO Coder team
basis: Documented workflow, checked against 0.8.0 source without a live Mercury run

title: Panes and docks: files, workers, and music
description: Show and hide a file browser, a live worker dashboard, and a focus radio beside the terminal conversation with one key each.
author: The CLIO Coder team
status: Experimental, off by default, needs Herdr

title: Keep named files with the models you chose
description: Declare which paths and tool results may reach which model targets, approve the policy, and see a request to any other destination refused.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Search by meaning and record worker runs
description: Index code, memory, and experiment folders with a local embedding model, and attach a redacted terminal recording to a worker's evidence.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Run CLIO Coder on a local model
description: Connect a local server with no account or key, check what CLIO Coder learned about it, and see what else to check if code must stay on your machine.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Submit a Slurm job through CLIO Coder
description: Declare the clio-kit Slurm server, install the skill, and let the agent submit and follow a job, with a confirmation before it reaches the scheduler.
author: The CLIO Coder team

title: Pre-register a benchmark before you measure
description: Use the experiment-protocol skill to lock thresholds, tolerances, and verdict conditions into a contract you commit before any result exists.
author: The CLIO Coder team
